summary: The article describes a trend as of September 2023 of families swapping screens for outdoor picnics and games, citing local parks, events and experts. It highlights benefits for physical health, mental health and family bonding, and describes community initiatives such as a tree-planting "Green Day". It closes by asking whether the trend will outlast the season and become a lasting tradition.
one_line: Families in autumn 2023 are trading screens for picnics and outdoor games at local parks, boosting health, bonding and community spirit.
key_facts: Jennifer and Connor Smith visited Meadowbrook Park on September 10, 2023, with their two young children and left their phones at home as a "tech detox".
Meadowbrook Park, with sprawling fields and aged oak trees providing shade, tops the list of sought-after family picnic locations.
Riverside Retreat, a spot by the water, has seen a consistent influx of families every weekend since early September.
Daniel Torres organized "The Grand Picnic Gathering" at Riverside Retreat on September 15, 2023, drawing record numbers.
The newly renovated Lakeview Gardens opened on September 20, 2023, and has placards teaching families about flora and fauna.
Game designer Marcie O'Brien introduced "Zones of Fortitude", a team-based game combining strategy and physical activity, at a community event on September 25, 2023.
Teenager Ethan Nguyen said he checked his phone every five minutes at first, then forgot it while playing Ultimate Frisbee with his cousins on October 1, 2023.
Child psychologist Jennifer Lucas said at a community health forum on October 6, 2023 that regular family outings can work wonders for mental health and family cohesion.
Dietitian Harriet Mills held a nutrition workshop at Maple Community Center on October 8, 2023, where parents and kids prepared healthy picnic snacks.
Amir Patel launched the "Green Day" initiative on October 12, 2023, in which families planted new trees and beautified communal picnic areas.
Classic games like hide-and-seek, tag and capture the flag remain favorites, along with sack races and tug-of-war in community parks.
The article questions whether the outdoor trend will last beyond a seasonal fad and become a firm tradition.
